scope: Full original Windows 7/8/8.1/10/11 x64 landscape including required mixed-architecture helpers, runtimes, services and drivers; own kernel/native execution; evidence remains scoped

stages.title: Original targets and baseline
stages.deliver: Pin original packages, inspect installer/payload/custom-action architectures, inventory static dependencies and native gaps, and freeze functional/performance protocols.
stages.how_and_why: Read-only PE/MSI analysis and exact source references avoid guessing from an x64 download label. Do not execute downloaded apps on the development host.
stages.acceptance: Version/hash inventory, installation-chain decisions, per-app task corpus, bounded performance protocol, source/native baseline, honest unknowns and complete public research delivery.

stages.title: Win64 loader and DLL environment
stages.deliver: Extend checked PE32+ mapping, relocations, imports/forwarders/delay imports, module lifetime and dependencies.
stages.how_and_why: Replace the current fixed eight-module/eight-MiB assumptions with explicit tested per-process quotas and demand-backed mappings, not unbounded allocations.
stages.acceptance: Original selected binaries load correctly with access violations, invalid images and missing required functions refused clearly; no GUI compatibility claim from loading alone.

stages.title: Processes, threads and exceptions
stages.deliver: Provide real Windows thread/TLS/wait/timer/exception behavior and child-process lifetime over isolated native processes.
stages.how_and_why: The existing one-thread console profile cannot safely substitute fake synchronization or success stubs for real behavior.
stages.acceptance: Concurrent original tasks and child processes behave correctly; faults/cancellation remain contained; repeated close releases owned resources.

stages.title: Files, paths and persistent settings
stages.deliver: Expand Unicode/case/path/share/delete/locking semantics, temporary files, environment and registry behavior.
stages.how_and_why: Translate Windows expectations to native storage with explicit access grants; keep user data separate from product ownership.
stages.acceptance: Selected app preferences/files survive independent starts; conflicting access and missing/denied paths return correct errors without corrupting data.

stages.title: Original Windows windows and messages
stages.deliver: Implement the required USER32 window/message/focus/input model and connect it to the native compositor.
stages.how_and_why: Run original application code and its actual message loop rather than recreate the target app as a native lookalike.
stages.acceptance: Original app windows visibly respond to input, focus, move/resize/minimize/close; ownership and modality do not operate the wrong app.
stages.publication_status: Complete under explicit owner scope: missing BrixCanvas documentation search/navigation is reported and nonblocking; native/media/download/content checks pass

stages.title: Drawing, text and common controls
stages.deliver: Implement required GDI/text/resources/menu/control/dialog behavior for the pinned applications.
stages.how_and_why: Share native drawing/fonts where semantics match, with bounded surfaces and dirty-region repaint; provider/name presence is not semantic compatibility.
stages.acceptance: Readable working original app interfaces at ordinary and named HiDPI profiles, with pixel and behavior evidence; no vendor GPU/DirectX claim.
stages.publication_status: Complete within explicit owner scope; advanced platform search/navigation remains reported, nonblocking and unqualified

stages.title: Open, save and clipboard interoperability
stages.deliver: Connect original app file dialogs, clipboard and actual document access with Files.
stages.how_and_why: Preserve requesting-window ownership and file semantics; original app data must be checked independently.
stages.acceptance: Open/edit/save/reopen, Unicode names, cancel and cross-app text clipboard tasks pass without lost or misdirected data.
stages.publication_status: Complete within the owner-approved content/layout scope: 594 pages, 385 exact-source articles, 4383 links, zero known broken targets and twelve unverified external references

stages.title: Reusable MSI execution
stages.deliver: Implement the selected packages' actual MSI standard actions, conditions/properties/component lifecycle, rollback and required custom actions.
stages.how_and_why: Replace the current one-digest console adapter with reusable behavior. Notepad++ MSI requires a real x64 WiX custom-action DLL and cmd/xcopy semantics; never skip it to claim successful installation.
stages.acceptance: Selected original MSI packages install/remove/reinstall correctly, including conditions, cancellation and fault recovery; missing mandatory actions refuse clearly.

stages.title: Original x64 EXE installers
stages.deliver: Execute pinned original AMD64 installer code, its GUI and required helpers/uninstaller.
stages.how_and_why: SumatraPDF provides a measured x64 route. The measured Notepad++ x64-labelled EXE is x86 and explicitly waits for M15; its original x64 MSI remains an M14 target.
stages.acceptance: At least one complete original x64 EXE installer chain and original MSI chains work; all required child binaries are inventoried and exercised.

stages.title: Environment contracts and compatibility reference laboratory
stages.deliver: Freeze environment identity, private storage/registry/component contracts, dependency records and versioned Windows reference probes.
stages.how_and_why: One ownership model prevents conflicting assumptions in loaders, runtime activation and installer UX.
stages.acceptance: Schemas, ownership/escape matrix, reference provenance, migration policy and all-three-route walkthroughs are reviewed; no runtime feature is claimed.
implementation_steps: Specify stable AppId, user, architecture, environment generation and owner identities; define which process/broker may create or change each identity.

Freeze a versioned bundle layout and manifest/transaction/dependency-record schema, including original source, component versions, graph edges, failures, permissions, private registry views, service instances and restart state.

Draw the boundary between private app components and native OS/kernel/device facilities. Ban cross-app DLL/runtime stores, link/dedup shortcuts and module cache reuse. Define minimal rebuildable shell/index records outside bundles.

Specify logical Windows paths and HKLM/HKCU/HKCR views, including x64/x86 redirection and architecture-correct component lookup. Include Win16/DOS requirements in the format without claiming their execution is implemented.

Define owner-bound context tickets and failure-event records for all three dependency entry routes. Ordinary installation remains primary; dependency targeting in a separately opened installer is under Advanced.

Build the versioned Windows 7/8/8.1/10/11 reference matrix and a traceable missing-contract register covering APIs, runtimes, components and drivers. Compare actual results, errors, ordering and side effects using owned probes.
Inventory legacy M14.8 state and design conservative migration/reinstallation rules. Ambiguous legacy ownership cannot be guessed or silently shared.
stages.reference_coverage: Published contracts and Windows host sample. Targeted version-specific guest captures are tracked by the implementation stages.

stages.title: Private execution, files, registry and process ownership
stages.deliver: Implement native owner context, private loader/files/registry/object views and required x86 helpers for x64 products.
stages.how_and_why: Enforce ownership at kernel/handle boundaries and preserve real Windows-visible semantics, errors and lifetime.
stages.acceptance: Native A/B private-copy/backing tests, inherited context, cross-owner rejection, delayed loading, mixed-architecture execution and cleanup pass.
implementation_steps: Attach immutable AppId/user/architecture/generation context to processes, threads, file/registry handles, memory objects and installer brokers. Inherit it across child creation, exceptions, cancellation and authorized privilege transitions; never trust a caller-editable environment variable as authority.

Implement private filesystem views for program/system/data/temp names. Resolve traversal, links, aliases, case, Unicode, locking and metadata inside the grant. Explicit external document grants do not grant foreign app roots.

Implement per-app durable registry machine/class/user stores, WOW64 views, enumeration, notifications, permissions and accurate errors. Project OS facts explicitly; do not use a global mutable Windows hive as a fallback.

Bind PE imports, delay/runtime DLL loads, manifests, activation contexts, API-set/system-module views and module caches to the correct environment. Loaded app components cannot come from a different AppId's backing pages.

Provide real process/thread/TLS/exception/wait/memory/identity behavior and owner-scoped named objects. Preserve original error and cleanup semantics; a namespace wrapper cannot turn unsupported work into successful no-ops.
Implement necessary x86 installer/helper execution and x64/x86 transitions for x64 products now. Respect 32-bit System32/SysWOW64 and registry views; standalone x86 product expansion remains M15.

Add bounded terminal-failure events at actual import/activation/helper boundaries. Record architecture, requested identity, final error and owner. Do not classify every failed intermediate search as a missing dependency.
Implement protected bundle metadata and minimal rebuildable native indexes; enforce owner-safe rename/move and stale-object rejection.

stages.title: Private runtimes, services and dependency activation
stages.deliver: Execute private runtimes, COM/services/helpers and transitive dependency activation, including real .NET family/version behavior.
stages.how_and_why: A private directory or registry version flag is not a working CLR or service; implement and test actual dependencies.
stages.acceptance: Original runtime/helper tasks activate correctly, late/optional failures are distinguished and two apps retain independent components and service state.
implementation_steps: Inventory runtime family/version/architecture requirements from manifests, managed metadata, configuration and real activation traces. Distinguish .NET Framework (including CLR 4 activation) from modern .NET, native C/C++ runtimes, scripting engines and Java or other app-required runtimes.

Implement required CLR hosting/activation, assembly/fusion binding and private framework/GAC/servicing views. Resolve the original runtime's own Windows API, file, registry and component dependencies without global reuse.
Implement private COM/OLE/WinRT registration and activation, including local/out-of-process servers and correct AppId inheritance through brokers.

Implement owner-scoped service instances, SCM behavior, RPC/IPC, pipes, helper programs, scripts and command environments. Same service/component names in two apps must not bind to the same app-owned running instance.

Provide the required networking, TLS/cryptography, authentication, data and identity semantics. External services and licensing are genuine integration requirements; their failure is not automatically a missing local runtime.

Add version-aware transitive dependency resolution and activation verification: identify required/optional features, conflicts, architecture mismatches and cycles. Another independently installed app cannot satisfy this graph.

Emit bounded evidence for late runtime/COM/service/helper failures. Separate missing components from corrupted installations, access errors, unavailable OS contracts and ordinary optional probes. Carry AppId through every event.
Start dependencies on demand where their semantics permit; honor explicitly authorized background services without starting all installed runtimes at boot.

stages.title: Owner-bound installation, dependency setup and maintenance
stages.deliver: Provide general original installers, owner-bound dependency setup, private durable inventory and install/update/repair/recovery/removal.
stages.how_and_why: All three user entry routes converge on one reviewed owner-bound transaction; ordinary standalone installation remains primary.
stages.acceptance: Original chains, explicit dependency target selection, nested/resumed setup, crash recovery and remove-A/run-B pass without a global dependency pool.
implementation_steps: Execute real MSI/MSP, EXE bootstrappers, MSIX/AppX and required custom actions, prerequisites, servicing and helper chains. Package semantics are general; application-name/digest allowlists are not the final compatibility model.

Ordinary installation creates a new AppId and standalone bundle. A separately opened installer exposes Install as dependency only in collapsed Advanced options, with explicit existing-app selection and target confirmation.

Accept owner-bound requests from automatic assistance and right-click Add dependency. Preserve the selected AppId through nested setup, downloads, helper/elevation brokers, services and restart/resume. Never infer permission solely from the most recently running or installed app.

Resolve dependency graphs, exact version/architecture constraints, sources, required features, disk cost, cycles and conflicts before mutation. Run each dependency's actual installer in the chosen environment, not another app's.

Track installed files, hives, assemblies, services, cached repair sources and external shell references by owner. Source downloads can be inputs; runtime operation may not depend on an external download or another bundle's cache.

Implement staging, journals, commit, verification, cancellation, rollback, repair, update, interrupted-operation recovery and safe uninstall. Private transactions live under the app root with preflight space bounds.
Handle active processes, authorized background services and reboot-required changes explicitly. Do not restart an app with unsaved work automatically.

Implement conservative legacy migration: move only attributable state or reinstall original sources. Raw directory deletion must leave no required dependency broken in other apps; reconcile stale launch references safely.

stages.title: Private app device access, driver ownership and acceleration
stages.deliver: Provide required driver/device contracts and real acceleration through native hardware mediation with attributable app contexts.
stages.how_and_why: Private app-driver files do not automatically isolate kernel privilege; separate component ownership from physical resource arbitration.
stages.acceptance: Real device work and reset/fault/teardown pass on declared profiles; removing A cannot remove B components or native platform drivers.
implementation_steps: Classify native platform drivers, app-private user-mode driver components and required foreign privileged driver interfaces. Give each component an owner, authority boundary, real device lifetime and implementation/test plan.

Store vendor app-specific DLLs, driver binaries, service registrations and configuration within their app environment. Do not silently install one shared vendor app driver or service to satisfy several application bundles.

Define the necessary WDM/WDF/NT-style binary structures, object, request, synchronization, memory/DMA, interrupt and lifecycle contracts. File isolation alone does not make a privileged driver safe or provide driver compatibility.

Mediate real physical devices through the own kernel. Bind clients, requests, callbacks, handles, GPU contexts/VRAM and access rights to the owning AppId. Hardware remains physical shared infrastructure, not a dependency copied into each folder or a reason to reuse another app's executable components.

Resolve device exclusivity, conflicting driver expectations, required global kernel semantics and privilege transitions explicitly. Required gaps remain implementation work; neither a false success nor an undisclosed global dependency fallback is permitted.

Implement actual graphics/compute/media/print/input/device operations and required virtualization interfaces. Discovery and framebuffer output alone do not establish acceleration or a foreign driver's successful operation.
Make app update/removal tear down only that app's device execution and references. Removing A cannot unload a native platform driver needed by B or remove B's separately owned vendor components.

stages.title: Desktop dependency workflows and original application interfaces
stages.deliver: Deliver automatic dependency assistance, right-click Add dependency and ordinary installer Advanced targeting with usable original interfaces.
stages.how_and_why: Use evidence from native activation boundaries; optional searches and unknown failures must not generate compulsory installation prompts.
stages.acceptance: All three native flows, late requests, default/Advanced behavior, keyboard access, source/target confirmation and ordinary/HiDPI rendering pass.
implementation_steps: Keep ordinary Open installer / Install app as the primary/default action. Put Install as dependency for an existing app in collapsed Advanced options. Even a recognized runtime installer must not silently replace this default.

Add right-click Add dependency to app launchers and installed-app management. Bind the actual AppId, display its name/location and let the user choose a source. Preserve keyboard access, focus, navigation and clear cancellation.

Implement automatic assistance only for attributable necessary dependency failures. Inspect static declarations and actual loader/runtime/component/ helper events, including requests after successful app launch. No continuous disk/process scanner and no modal prompt for every failed optional probe.

Present the requested component, runtime family/version/architecture, requesting app, evidence, source, installed/temporary disk cost and exact intended action before consent. Do not promise a package fixes an unknown error; offer diagnostics/manual selection when confidence is insufficient.

Implement Advanced target selection with searchable app names and distinct identities for duplicates. Recent requests may be suggestions inside that workflow; no selection based solely on last foreground app.

Make all three routes converge on one transaction and progress/cancel/ retry/recovery view. Distinguish missing, incompatible, installed and verified components. Restart the original app only with appropriate consent.
Provide per-app dependency details, diagnostics and version/update/removal controls without exposing helpers as unrelated default desktop clutter.

Complete needed Windows controls, fonts, DPI, international input, accessibility, COM shell integration, shortcuts, associations, clipboard, printing and Open/Save interactions with correct owner/message semantics.

stages.title: Independent app composition, broad compatibility and stability
stages.deliver: Validate broad original workloads, private A/B independence, version behavior, required integrations, stability and recovery.
stages.how_and_why: Contract probes find causes; diverse original apps and repeated concurrent lifecycles verify composition without an app whitelist.
stages.acceptance: Original install/start/use/update/repair/remove tasks and fault/concurrency cases pass with physical ownership proof; necessary unresolved work stays explicit.
implementation_steps: Build a contract-driven original-software corpus spanning installer families, runtimes, services, helper chains, COM, device requirements and relevant Windows 7/8/8.1/10/11 behavior. Named apps remain fixtures, not a whitelist.

Run the mandatory A/B independence matrix with identical dependency names, hashes and versions, and with deliberately conflicting versions. Inspect physical ownership and actual execution, not just separate displayed folders.

Exercise install/start/use/close/update/repair/remove, cold restarts, concurrent execution, authorized background services and long-duration use. After every destructive A operation verify B's bytes/state and actual work.
Test late runtime requests, separately opened installers, Advanced targeting, context-menu addition, nested setup, resumed downloads and stale owner tickets.

Inject storage exhaustion, power loss, bad source/version/architecture, dependency cycles, failed activation, process/service crashes and device resets. Verify recoverable transitions and preserved personal documents.

Test cross-app escape attempts through paths/links, hives, module/assembly caches, named objects, brokers, service names and shared repair stores. Include multiuser identities, bundle relocation and duplicate imports.

Cover required external services, licences, trust/attestation, Windows version quirks and vendor integration. Private packaging does not implement these contracts or justify dropping necessary applications from scope.
Produce per-task compatibility evidence, unresolved-contract register, root-cause fixes and migration/reinstallation results for legacy M14.8 state.

stages.title: Whole-system optimization and independent-bundle release
stages.deliver: Measure and optimize the whole system without cross-app dependency sharing, then qualify exact final release media and publication.
stages.how_and_why: Optimize demand loading, bounded private caches and event-driven work; report duplicated disk/private RAM costs rather than hiding them through sharing.
stages.acceptance: Functional/resource budgets, independent copies, all-three-routes, A/B removal safety and exact source/media/download/website evidence agree.
implementation_steps: Measure cold/warm launch-to-interactive time, real app computation, total CPU/idle work, private/peak/retained RAM, input latency and broker/kernel costs. Measure actual filesystem and block bytes/requests/flushes, drained writeback, duplicate installed footprint and update/rollback peak storage.

Preserve independent installed copies for identical dependencies. Audit filesystem backing, module caches and physical app-code mappings; reject cross-app hard links, reflinks, deduplicated runtime stores or page coalescing.

Optimize demand loading, app-local indexes/caches, bounded buffers, metadata lookup, verification scheduling, on-demand services and event-driven waits. Do not introduce a permanent dependency scanner or global runtime daemon that makes app removal unsafe.

Attribute kernel/platform shared infrastructure separately from private dependency costs. Include all compatibility/device work in whole-system measurements; do not compare configured guest RAM with process use.

Preserve seven cold/seven warm sample protocols and twenty repeated lifecycle/resource checks where applicable. Record raw samples, median/p95, cache limitations, workload/version identities and reproducible budgets.

Resolve unexplained retained allocations and regression thresholds before release. Investigate the M14.8 removal measurement's four unattributed pages; do not label them a known cache or assume their cause.

Freeze compiled inputs and artifacts; rerun the full native, original-app, A/B independence, all-three-routes, recovery, hardware and physical rendering corpus on matching release media. Update stage-number tooling for M14.16.

Publish matching ISO/USB/VMware media, source/licence provenance, scope, tutorials and private-dependency workflows. Independently download assets and verify actual website content, routes, source links and current homepage.

publication_status: Native/source/media and twenty public asset downloads passed. Native homepage Save blocked; article content verified separately.

planning_revision.scope: Windows independent app environments; x64, required x86 helpers, planned standalone x86 and Win16/DOS
